decisions.decision: D-1: REQ-P22-05 encodes Cleveland & McGill's REAL 6-rank ordering WITH ties, not a 7-item strict order. Test asserts rank(a) <= rank(b), never a strict total order.
decisions.rationale: Independent primary-source read found the paper's p.536 list ties length/direction/angle at rank 3, and p.537 states 'there is not enough information to separate the ties'. Heer & Bostock p.206 independently report angle was NOT worse than length. The length>angle link the test would have asserted has no support in EITHER cited paper. Also: 'density' is absent from the 1984 paper entirely; 'curvature' and 'shading' were silently dropped from their tied ranks.

decisions.decision: D-2: REQ-P22-02 adopts Wilke's actual 10 uncertainty marks from section 5.6, not the four originally proposed.
decisions.rationale: 'fan chart' appears nowhere in the entire book (verified against the full-text search index, all 34 pages). 'gradient CI band' is not Wilke's term — he has two DISTINCT marks: 'confidence strips' (continuous fade, Fig 16.9e) and 'graded confidence band' (nested levels, Fig 16.17). 'half-eye' is real but lives in section 5.6, not ch.16. Paradigm symmetry IS strongly confirmed.

decisions.decision: D-3: Attribute the FT nine-category axis and write our own descriptions; never vendor the poster PDF or copy its blurbs. Drop any 'exhaustive' claim resting on the FT.
decisions.rationale: The 'FT Visual Vocabulary is MIT-licensed' claim is WRONG — the repo is MIT but the FT carves out its content in writing, twice: 'does not cover any FT content ... all rights reserved'. The poster also disclaims exhaustiveness in its own words.

decisions.decision: D-4: dual_axis_line cites 'Muth 2018, as amended July 2026' and scopes its reason string to a general audience.
decisions.rationale: Datawrapper publicly reversed its position in July 2026 ('we've changed our minds'), carving out expert users (finance) while still holding that general audiences misread these charts. The ban stands as a deliberate DSX position, not an appeal to a softened claim.
